Putting it on your phone

How to open Roast, keep it on your home screen like any other app, decide whether you want an account, and what happens when there is no signal.

On this pageWhat this part is forOpen it and keep it on your home screenWith or without an accountWorking with no signal

What this part is for

Roast is a web app. It lives at an address, like a website, but once it has opened on your phone it keeps a copy of itself so it opens fast and keeps working without a network. This chapter gets it onto your phone and helps you choose between keeping records only on this phone or also in a private account.

Open it and keep it on your home screen

  1. Open Chrome (Android) or Safari (iPhone) and go to roast.koffykraft.coffee. The first time, Roast opens on Home. You will see the words Coffee, from farm to cup.

  2. Put it on your home screen. On an iPhone: tap the Share button at the bottom of Safari, then Add to Home Screen. On Android: tap the ⋮ menu at the top right of Chrome, then Add to home screen. These menus belong to your phone's browser, not to Roast, so their words can differ a little between phones.

  3. Open Roast from the new icon. It now opens on its own, without the browser's address bar.

Tip

Open it once while you have a signal. That is when the phone keeps its copy of the app. After that it opens even in airplane mode.

With or without an account

You can use everything in Roast without an account. The difference is where your records are kept.

No accountSigned in
Where records liveOnly on this phoneOn this phone and in your private account
Another phone sees themNoYes, once you sign in there with the same email
If the phone is lost or resetGone, unless you saved a backup fileStill in your account
What it costsNothingNothing

Keep going without an account

  1. Tap the round person button at the top right, then Account and sign-in.

  2. Under Continue without an account, tap Continue locally. Nothing else is needed.

Sign in with your email

There is no password. Each time you sign in, Roast emails you a 6-digit code.

  1. On the Account page, find Private cloud account. Type your email in the Email box.

  2. Read the privacy notice (the link is in the sentence beside the tick box). It says what is kept, for how long, and what happens to your records if KoffyKraft closes. If you agree, tick the box.

  3. Tap Send sign-in code. You will see 6-digit code sent to and your email, and a new box for the code.

  4. Open your email, find the sign-in email, and type the 6 digits into the 6-digit code box.

  5. Tap Verify & sign in. The page reloads and you are signed in.

When you are signed in and online, records already on this phone go to your account, and records made on your other phones come in.

Watch out

If you tap Send sign-in code without ticking the box, nothing is sent and the page asks you to read and tick the privacy notice first. After a code is sent, the button rests for 30 seconds before it will send another, so wait for the first email before tapping again. Check your spam folder if it has not arrived.

Tip

Staff who enter records for you can sign in on their own phone with the same account email. Each record still shows who entered it.

Working with no signal

Roast is built for hill farms, drying yards and store rooms where the signal comes and goes.

  • Everything you enter is saved on the phone first. On Origin you will see Saved on this device under the page name, and a saved record shows On this phone.
  • Find works with no signal. It searches the records on this phone.
  • The ? still works. With a signal it opens the full guide on koffykraft.coffee. Without one, it opens the guide kept inside the app.
  • New versions arrive by themselves. The App version card on Account has Check for updates if you want to look now.
Watch out

A few things need the internet because they ask a server: signing in, the land check on a plot, and fetching weather. The app tells you plainly when it needs a connection; nothing you typed is lost.

Watch out

If you use Roast without an account, your records live only in this phone's browser. Clearing the browser's data, or removing the app from the phone, removes them too. Save a backup file now and then. When one is due, Now shows a Keep a copy card that takes you there: after 14 days when your records are only on this phone, after 30 when you are signed in. On Account, Backup reminder lets you change this to weekly, after each save, or off.

Why it matters

Records you cannot lose are records you can trust. Working on the phone first means a bad signal never stops a harvest being written down; an account or a backup file means a lost phone never takes a season's records with it.
